L2t: In a lease-to-holdover situation like this, the tenant's original entry was lawful and with the owner's permission, so adverse possession cannot begin until the possession becomes hostile.
L3t: Because the widow's death did not end the lease or change the tenant's character as a permissive occupant, the tenant's possession only became hostile once he stopped paying rent and subjectively regarded himself as no longer having permission to be there.
L4t: The adverse possession period began when the tenant, having stopped paying rent, subjectively believed he no longer had permission to possess the cottage.
L2f: Adverse possession doctrine generally disregards the possessor's state of mind and looks only at how long the land was physically occupied, regardless of how the occupant originally entered.
L3f: A landlord's death automatically extinguishes a lease and converts the tenant into a trespasser at that moment, so the tenant's possession was no longer permissive from then on.
L4f: The adverse possession period began to run when the widow died, because that ended the lease and the tenant's permission.
cand_true: When the tenant subjectively believed he no longer had permission to possess the cottage
cand_wrong2: When the Boy Scouts of America discovered their claim to ownership in 2009
